I absolutely love my ice maker!  I have worked it pretty hard over the last year.  In fact, my sister loves it so much that I purchased one for her birthday.  We live in the country where even with a water softener it doesn't get all the minerals out of the water.  So, I use gallon jugs of drinking water and refill them at the store.  Each time I make ice it uses around a half gallon of water.  Of course, depending on the size of cubes you make there may be differences in the amount of ice that is made.  For me, I use the largest cubes and  have about 3 gallon bags of ice.  (I would freeze the ice after making it.  It will stick together, so you may want to check it periodically; or, you can break it loose later.  Personally, I use the back of an ice cream scoop and break the ice loose).  One of my favorite things about this ice maker is that the ice is a softer consistency.  It crushes easily for smoothies, margaritas.  It's soft enough for kids with sore throats or just adding juice for a cool summer drink.  If you love eating ice; this ice maker is for you! .
The ice melts quickly so you need to use it within 20 mins of making. If you try to freeze it, then they freeze together and are useless.

Since we are in a rental home we didn't get to choose our refrigerator and ended up with one that doesn't have an ice maker. After months of buying bags of ice and having it take up valuable freezer space we decided to get one of these after talking to a friend that has one. It is absolutely worth the money spent to have my freezer space cleared up and to be able to make as much or as little ice as we need! No more frantic trips to the gas station when we have company over and are low on ice. The ice cubes are a nice size and there is no worry of spilling the tray of water on the way to the freezer with the typical ice cube trays. I love that we can take it camping and also to anywhere else we move to. Good quality and exactly as described, I didn't have any of the problems that other reviewers have had. Would highly recommend for anyone that rents, camps or has a fridge that doesn't make ice.

I bought this to test out what induction cooking is like as we were considering buying an in-counter cooktop. I love the idea of induction cooking—I remember as a kid (when induction was crazy expensive) I thought it was so Star Trek that I could barely wait the 30 years it would take for me to be in a position to buy a stovetop. And better yet, it doesn't produce the excess heat waste that any other power source does, so it is greener *and* more pleasant to use. (Gas and electric pump waste heat out pretty bad, and to double the inefficiency, that generally means you air conditioner will be doing extra duty.)

The promise of precision cooking and near-immediate temperature changes is really exciting, but this model absolutely doesn't live up. I've tested with laser thermometers and plain boil tests in a variety of good pans, and this one has bad hot-spots and cold spots; adjusting the temperature doesn't take effect quickly, even if you change it by a lot; and anything above 3 or 4 (on a scale of TEN) is way too hot for most anything except nuking a pot of water.

I DO UNDERSTAND that an inexpensive tabletop model could never be a very accurate example of what cooking on a "real" Bertazzoni or Wolf or GE cooktop or range would be like. Nevertheless, I was hoping this would be good enough to give us the confidence of buying an expensive induction cooktop, and it did the opposite.

My lament is that dual-heat cooktops just aren't available
